steps.description: Write the report leading with the answer to the research question, then the evidence. plan.title: Heart RNA-seq: genotype x treatment interaction (KO vs WT, drug vs vehicle)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question — does the drug act differently in the KO than in the WT — is a genotype x treatment interaction on a balanced 2x2 design: 16 human heart samples (metadata.csv, 16 x 4: genotype WT/KO, treatment vehicle/drug, condition), 4 replicates per cell, against a 12000-gene raw count matrix from Salmon (counts.csv, 12000 x 17: gene id column + 16 sample columns). All scripts are Python per the user constraint, so the count model is fitted with PyDESeq2 0.5.4 (present in the sandbox), which implements the DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors, the negative binomial GLM, the Wald test and shrinkage; no R is used anywhere.

T1S1 runs the sample structure QC before any test: blind variance-stabilizing transform, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap and library sizes, coloured by genotype, treatment and the four condition cells. This is the step that would expose a swapped label or an outlier cell before the interaction is fitted; with 4 replicates per cell an outlier is not something the model can absorb quietly.

T1S2 fits the design ~genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment with explicit reference levels (genotype WT, treatment vehicle) on genes passing the minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=4 samples, the smallest group size), leaving independent filtering to do the rest at alpha 0.05. The interaction coefficient is the direct answer to the question; because both factors have two levels it is a single Wald-testable coefficient. T1S3 then produces the three results the question actually needs side by side per gene: the drug effect within WT, the drug effect within KO, and the interaction contrast (the difference of differences), each with BH adjustment applied within contrast, ashr-style shrunken log2 fold changes for ranking, and the p-value histogram, MA and dispersion diagnostics.

Two honesty constraints are written into the plan. First, the profile says the counts are Salmon gene-level output but does not record whether the length correction was applied, and there are no per-sample quant.sf files or an average-transcript-length table in the inputs; the model is therefore fitted on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and the report must state that the offset is lost and that a shift in isoform usage can appear as differential expression. Second, an interaction coefficient is a difference of differences with a large standard error; at 4 replicates per cell power is low, so a short list — or an empty one — at padj < 0.05 is an expected outcome and must be reported as low power rather than as evidence of no genotype-dependent drug effect. T1S4 adds an optional over-representation check of the interaction genes against human WikiPathways (present in the reference store at /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human) purely as annotation; if too few genes are significant, that step reports the shortfall instead of forcing an enrichment.

steps.method: VST-blind PCA and sample distance heatmap
median-of-ratios size factors inside the model
two-factor design with interaction, explicit reference levels
DESeq2 Wald test on the genotype:treatment interaction coefficient plus simple effects
ashr shrinkage of the log2 fold change
Benjamini-Hochberg within contrast with independent filtering
interaction report with simple effects, MA and dispersion plots, reproducibility record
Low count filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples

acceptance_criteria: Three named contrasts are reported side by side per gene: drug-vs-vehicle in WT, drug-vs-vehicle in KO, and the interaction (difference of differences), with the reference levels named beside the table
Each contrast carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, pvalue and BH-adjusted padj; ranking and plots use the shrunken value
BH adjustment is applied within each contrast, and the report states FDR holds per contrast not across contrasts
Independent filtering is on with alpha = 0.05 passed to the results call; genes with NA padj from filtering are counted separately from those NA from the outlier flag
A p-value histogram is produced per contrast before adjustment, with its shape described (flat / right-skewed / irregular)
MA plots per contrast and the dispersion plot are produced
Gene counts are reported per contrast: n tested, n significant at padj < 0.05, n NA

If the interaction contrast yields few or zero significant genes, the output states this is consistent with the low power of a difference-of-differences at n=4 per cell and does not claim absence of a genotype-dependent drug effect
The shrinkage estimator actually used for each contrast is named; any substitution from ashr is stated explicitly
constraints: Use Python only — PyDESeq2 and statsmodels; no R
alpha = 0.05, adjustment = Benjamini-Hochberg, applied within contrast
independent_filtering = true, with the same alpha passed to the results call
Select significant genes by adjusted p-value only — never by unadjusted p-value and never by fold change alone
Report both the shrunken and the unshrunken log2 fold change; rank on the shrunken value
If a minimum effect size is wanted, test against it with an lfcThreshold inside the model rather than filtering the estimates post hoc; if no threshold is applied, say so
Name the reference levels (genotype = WT, treatment = vehicle) beside every table
Set and record a random seed for any stochastic step
caveats: The interaction coefficient is a difference of differences with a large standard error; with 4 replicates per cell power is low and a short or empty significant list is an expected outcome, not evidence of no differential drug action
A gene significant for the interaction but not for either simple effect, or vice versa, is common and must be interpreted from the three columns together
The length offset is absent (see T1S2): a shift in isoform usage can present here as differential expression — carry this caveat into the written report
Independent filtering changes the set of genes carried into the BH adjustment, so per-contrast tested-gene counts will differ between contrasts

steps.name: Pathway annotation of the interaction genes
steps.question: Which human pathways are over-represented among the genes whose drug response differs between KO and WT, and how do they compare with the pathways moved by the drug within each genotype?
steps.context: Takes the three result tables from T1S3. This is an annotation layer on top of the answer, not the answer itself: the research question is answered by the interaction test. Reference data needed: a human pathway gene-set collection with HGNC gene symbols — the reference store currently holds human WikiPathways (2026.07.10) as a GMT whose first field is '%'-delimited (name, WikiPathways ID, species) and whose members are HGNC symbols.
steps.description: Resolve a human pathway gene-set collection from the reference store and confirm its organism is human before use. Map the gene identifiers of the count matrix to the identifier space of the collection, reporting the mapping rate; if the counts carry Ensembl or Entrez identifiers, use the human UniProt ID-mapping resource in the store to translate, and report how many of the tested genes could not be mapped. Run over-representation analysis (gseapy enrichr-style ORA against the local GMT, hypergeometric with BH adjustment) on the significant interaction genes at padj < 0.05, with the universe restricted to the genes actually tested in T1S3 — not all 12000 input genes. Separately run a rank-based GSEA (gseapy prerank) on all tested genes ranked by the Wald statistic of the interaction contrast, which does not depend on a significance cutoff and is the more informative analysis if the significant list is short. Do the same prerank for the two simple-effect contrasts so the pathways of the WT drug response, the KO drug response and their difference can be compared. Set and record the permutation seed.
acceptance_criteria: The pathway collection used is named with its organism (human) and version, and confirmed to match the dataset organism before any enrichment runs
Gene identifier mapping rate to the collection's identifier space is reported, with the count of unmapped tested genes
ORA on the significant interaction genes uses the T1S3 tested-gene set as the universe, with BH-adjusted p-values
A rank-based GSEA on the interaction Wald statistic across all tested genes is reported, with the permutation seed recorded
Prerank results for the WT and KO drug-response contrasts are reported alongside, so the three can be compared
If fewer than 10 genes are significant for the interaction, the step reports the shortfall and relies on the rank-based result rather than forcing an ORA
If no suitable human pathway collection is available at run time, the step reports that plainly and the analysis stands on T1S3 without pathway annotation
constraints: Use Python only — gseapy and/or decoupler; no R
The ORA universe is the set of genes tested in T1S3, not the full 12000-gene input matrix
The pathway collection must be human; do not substitute the mouse or rat collection
Rank the prerank input by the Wald test statistic, not by the fold change
Record the permutation seed and the collection version in the output
caveats: This step is annotation, not the answer: an empty or uninformative enrichment does not weaken the interaction result from T1S3
With a potentially short interaction gene list, ORA is underpowered and its p-values should be read as descriptive

Enrichment on an interaction statistic is harder to interpret than on a simple contrast — a pathway enriched here means the drug response in that pathway differs by genotype, not that the pathway is up or down

grounding.reason: Optional annotation layer beyond the differential expression question the procedure covered; planned from general practice (ORA universe restricted to tested genes, rank-based GSEA on the test statistic) and marked as non-essential to the research question

steps.name: Interaction report and reproducibility record
steps.question: Stated plainly: does the drug act differently in the KO than in the WT heart samples, and how strong is that evidence given 4 replicates per cell?
steps.context: Assembles T1S1-T1S4 into one written report. The audience needs the direct answer, the evidence, and the limits of the evidence in that order.
steps.description: Write the report leading with the answer to the research question, then the evidence. Include: the design formula and the explicit reference levels (genotype WT, treatment vehicle); the three contrasts with counts of tested and significant genes at padj < 0.05; the merged gene table with the WT drug effect, the KO drug effect and the interaction side by side, ranked by shrunken interaction log2 fold change; the QC findings from T1S1 including any flagged sample; the MA plots, dispersion plot and p-value histograms; the pathway annotation from T1S4 if it produced anything. State the limitations explicitly and without softening: (a) 4 replicates per cell gives low power for a difference of differences, so a short significant list is uninformative about the absence of an effect; (b) the Salmon counts were used as delivered with no transcript-length offset because no quantification files or length table were supplied, so isoform-usage shifts can present as differential expression; (c) FDR is controlled within each contrast, not across the three. Close with a reproducibility record: Python and package versions (pydeseq2, gseapy, numpy, pandas, statsmodels), the seeds used, the pathway collection version, and the exact filter and alpha settings.
acceptance_criteria: The report opens with a direct answer to whether the drug acts differently in KO than WT, qualified by the strength of evidence
Design formula, reference levels, filter settings (min_count 10, min_samples 4) and alpha (0.05) are stated before the gene tables
Per-contrast counts of tested genes, significant genes and NA-padj genes with their cause are given
The three limitations (low interaction power at n=4, missing length offset, per-contrast FDR) are stated explicitly in the report body
A reproducibility record with package versions, seeds and the pathway collection version is included
No claim is made that exceeds what the adjusted p-values support
constraints: Use Python only for any figure or table regeneration
Do not restate an exploratory signal as a conclusion
Report the shrunken and unshrunken log2 fold change with lfcSE for every reported gene
Name the reference levels wherever a fold change direction is stated
caveats: If the interaction yields no significant genes, the correct conclusion is that this design did not detect a genotype-dependent drug effect at the sample size available — not that none exists

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report step as such; its content follows the reporting claims returned by the procedure (interaction report side by side, shrunken and unshrunken effects, fit diagnostics, method and reproducibility fields)

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
